paper_title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops. As new evidence revises the topology, ReWeave reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width. Across tasks, matching verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups ($0.34\times$ full concatenation) within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. ReWeave improves held-out success from 89.00% to 98.75% on LIBERO-PRO and from 25.50% to 58.25% on RoboDojo, while uncovering retained progress in 89% of 159 failed RoboDojo development trials and translating stronger offline reasoning into higher online performance. On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, the shared harness reaches 51.3% success versus 41.3% for direct distillation, rising to 75.0% after continual learning.

sections.content: harness reaches 51.3%. Long-horizon manipulation depends on establishing physical conditions needed by downstream actions [15, 20]. Plausible high-level plans often fail because key physical requirements, such as contact stability, clearance margins, and assembly tolerances, emerge only during execution. These dynamics cannot be anticipated priori, making physical trial-and-error necessary yet costly. Maximizing what each trial teaches is thus vital for adaptation and reuse. Recent work repairs programs and evolves skills from execution feedback [5, 22, 28], distills playbooks [17], or organizes repairs with workflow graphs [29]. These advances leave distinct question: when new evidence changes our understanding of physical prerequisite, how should already collected trials be reassessed? Keeping their interpretation fixed can hide partial progress behind failure labels. Likewise, storing successful routine does not identify which local mechanism another task needs. Revisable dependencies connect retrospective credit, harness revision, and conditionbased transfer  (Fig. 1)  . Research question. How can we continually revise physical task understanding through interaction to reinterpret experience, improve agent harnesses, and transfer mechanisms across tasks? [Challenge 1] Nominal task plans mask latent physical bottlenecks [Sec. 3.2.1]. Execution can expose missing physical requirements. Revised understanding calls for rereading past trials to assess retained progress. [Challenge 2] Diagnosing bottleneck does not reveal remedy [Sec. 3.2.2]. Context, action routines, and feedback loops are coupled. Several edits can address one failure, but each needs physical validation. [Challenge 3] Task-specific success does not guarantee transfer [Sec. 3.2.3]. Specialists depend on their scenes and objects. New tasks may need one local mechanism or parts from several specialists, each with prerequisites. We introduce ReWeave, which uses an emergent physical task topology to make changes in task understanding explicit  (Fig. 2)  . It links physical dependencies and alternative routes to evidence and harness mechanisms. Beyond using old traces to propose repairs, topology revision changes how the same archived trials are credited and compared (Challenge 1). Reprojected progress and bottlenecks then guide harness search (Challenge 2). Across tasks, matching verified transition effects to unmet conditions identifies which specialist mechanisms to combine in shared harness for transfer and continual learning (Challenge 3). On LIBERO-PRO and RoboDojo, ReWeave achieves strong performance: 98.75% and 58.25% SR, gains of 9.75 and 32.75 points over 𝐻0, respectively. Re-reading 159 failed RoboDojo development trials on their final topologies finds retained progress in 89% (median 0.33; Fig. 3). We introduce an emergent representation of task understanding that connects physical dependencies, alternative routes, execution evidence, and reusable harness mechanisms. Topology-Guided Harness Optimization. We develop joint harness optimization guided by emergent task understanding and the physical cost of further search. Topology-Guided Meta-Distillation. We develop metadistillation matching specialist mechanisms to unmet conditions for cross-task consolidation and transfer.

sections.content: 8 ReWeave co-optimizes task understanding and an agent harness without weight updates. Transitions bind verified conditions, witnesses, and code; revised topologies re-score archived trials to guide optimization and transfer. Experiments show that this re-reading reveals progress in failed trials and supports reuse across tasks. The source code is publicly available. Limitations. Topology inference depends on observable traces, and ambiguous contacts can delay edge resolution. Optimization requires physical trials and model calls. Agent reasoning adds execution latency, limiting use in time-sensitive settings; transfer remains uneven across the hardest tasks in the initial eight-source setting.
